For C09, the otherwise unstated boundary ceiling is execution; the fixed rejection projection makes this input field unavailable in the result.

Unless a row explicitly states otherwise, the boundary finding has empty reasons and limitations. Each counter entry introduced by a row has empty basis_refs, reasons, and limitations except for values explicitly stated in that row. A row that introduces counter entries replaces the common not-supplied entry. Profile-gap entries have no current_scope_capability unless explicitly stated. In C12, the composed execution finding carries L-boundary inherited from the stated premise.

Unless a row explicitly overrides its basis-reference set, each base finding has a singleton basis-reference set whose local name is O for observation, I for intent, N for invocation, and E for execution. The PROV(execution) finding uses P(E). IV findings for observation, intent, invocation, and execution use V(O), V(I), V(N), and V(E), respectively. Each local name denotes the profile-scoped atom under the fixture profile defined below. These are exact basis-reference names, not aliases of the full base or qualifier names. C11 and C12 instead use their explicitly stated execution basis-reference set {s1,s2,adj,w}.

This local fixture identity is not an IANA registration or a network locator. This paragraph completely defines its revision: P_COUNTER_FAIL is registered in the substantive category, is applicable to C15's counter entry, and means that the fixture's assessment found the stated material counter-evidence unresolved. It adds no status, evidence, or independent acceptance condition. The profile defines no recorder-relation tokens or scope-extension names. Opaque fixture atoms compare by exact Unicode scalar text; a displayed basis reference or limitation denotes the ordered pair of this profile identity and its displayed local name. No URI, case, or Unicode normalization is implicit. A harness MUST NOT infer an applied profile solely from a token or basis reference. An executable representation pins these profile contents and its own encoding rules in its manifest.

section.name: Security Considerations
section.t: WEXP limits inference; it does not make a dishonest or compromised witness honest. A false boundary assertion, malicious mapping profile, compromised signer, or colluding evidence evaluator can manufacture normalized findings unless the evaluation context independently constrains those actors.

Authenticity is not truth. A valid signature establishes that bytes verify under a key. Key-to-identity binding attributes the assertion. Neither establishes that the action occurred, that the signer controlled the claimed boundary, or that the signer was authorized.

Reference integrity is not semantic support. A digest can bind an appraisal input to artifact bytes. It does not establish the artifact's type, exact-action coverage, accepted root, or independence. Qualifier support requires the exact profile predicate in .

Boundary grounding. A declared boundary can be false. An accept or downgrade appraisal preserves whether it was asserted, attributed, attested, or not evaluated. A reject appraisal instead uses the fixed projection in , with boundary_grounding = unavailable. Result carriers and presentation profiles preserve the reported grounding without promoting it to a stronger class. Relying parties MUST NOT erase this distinction.
Self-report. A self-report can support a report about what the actor asserted. It does not provide third-party non-repudiation merely because its content base is deep or its bytes are signed.

Independent verification. Independence is profile- and context-relative. Different keys or roots can remain under common administrative control, while a shared public root does not necessarily destroy operational independence. A passing IV finding needs an explicit assessment basis.
Counter-evidence. Unresolved material counter-evidence blocks acceptance. No supplied counter-evidence is not proof that none exists.

Coverage and nonoccurrence. A set of valid records can be incomplete. A missing record can reflect omission, capture failure, refusal to emit, loss, or an action that never occurred. WEXP Core does not distinguish those cases without positive profile-defined evidence.

Composition. Composition is a common inflation point. Exact premises, bindings, warrants, and limitation inheritance are required. A chain appraisal cannot be used as evidence for a terminal effect unless a separate predicate establishes that exact claim.

Evaluation context. Trust anchors, profile versions, policies, evaluation time, revocation state, and appraiser capabilities affect findings. An accept or downgrade appraisal carries the evaluation context so that the result is not detached from those dependencies. A reject appraisal instead uses the fixed projection in , with evaluation_context = unavailable. A result carrier can retain request provenance alongside a rejection, but that provenance is not the Core evaluation context and does not alter the fixed rejection projection.

Privacy. Even opaque targets, basis references, reason codes, and timing information can enable correlation. Carrier and evidence profiles should minimize disclosure and state the confidentiality properties of any commitments they use.

section.name: IANA Considerations
section.t: This document requests creation of a "Witnessed Execution Protocol (WEXP)" registry group containing a "WEXP Appraisal Reason Codes" registry. The registration policy is Specification Required as defined by . Each entry contains a token, category (fatal, substantive, or evaluation-gap), default verdict effect, current-scope capability (none, authenticity, or composition), and reference. Tokens begin with an uppercase ASCII letter and contain only uppercase ASCII letters, digits, and underscores. Token comparison is case-sensitive. No particular prefix, including E_, is required. This registration syntax does not prescribe a carrier encoding or limit on artifact size.

The current-scope capability column is part of the immutable registration semantics resolved under . Its value is none for every fatal or substantive token, and for an evaluation-gap token that is not permitted with current_scope_capability. An evaluation-gap registration with value authenticity or composition permits that marker only for the named capability. The referenced specification defines the exact assessment represented by that binding. Initially, E_COMPOSITION_NOT_EVALUATED is bound to composition; no other initial token is permitted with that marker. An applicable profile registration supplies any additional binding, including a token for authenticity. A marker naming a different capability or a token without such a binding produces E_PROFILE_MAPPING_INVALID.

Initial entries are shown below; the reference for every initial entry is this document. The default effect describes the condition that generates the diagnostic, not a verdict computed from token presence alone. The verdict procedure in is authoritative. In particular, a reason carried by a finding or a profile-supplied evaluation gap can coexist with accept; its presence does not negate a passing exact predicate. An unevaluated counter entry affecting the asserted claim blocks acceptance even when its materiality has not been established.

The remaining initial fatal tokens can be supplied only under the exact meanings and structurally usable-input rule in that section. Carrier-specific parse or extension errors are outside this Core registry and are neither aliases nor automatic mappings to Core tokens.

The Designated Expert should verify the token syntax and uniqueness, one unambiguous condition, a deterministic category and default effect, a valid current-scope capability value and its consistency with the category and referenced assessment, and a stable public specification. Changing the meaning, category, or current-scope capability of an existing token requires a new token; an existing registration is not reinterpreted by an incompatible update. A registration that would create claim support from an evaluation capability, display label, boundary name, or artifact presence should be rejected.

section.name: Compatibility and Migration
section.t: The Internet-Draft revision, Core semantics version, profile revision, and executable-corpus identity are separate versioned objects. This document defines only wexp-core-2. A multi-version implementation selects an explicit semantic procedure before invoking it; it does not relabel a wexp-core-1 input or silently apply these rules to a historical result.

The version change reflects ingress differences. Core-01 contained a conflict between its general counter-evidence scope rule and C14; this revision preserves C14's entry-specific intent without claiming that all Core-01 readers agreed. It also makes the previously unresolved single-role scope case an explicit mapping rejection and states the shared-role interpretation. Those choices can change admission for the same findings. Unchanged support algebra does not make the whole contract interchangeable.

Existing Core-01 fixtures, source bytes, results, and issue records retain their identities. The new common fixture context changes the complete logical inputs and non-reject outputs, even where verdicts and supported sets remain the same. Representations of this revision therefore use new manifests and expectations. A Core-01 conformance or interoperability result is not evidence of conformance to this revision without a separately recorded evaluation.
